paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this letter. Peter writes to exiles, folks far from home, and he doesn't start with their problems. He starts with praise: "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ!" (1 Peter 1:3). By His great mercy, God has given them new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead (1 Peter 1:3).

That hope isn't a wish, and it isn't hanging by a thread. Peter says the inheritance is "imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you," and that through faith they are "shielded by God's power" (1 Peter 1:4-5). Trials still come, and Peter says so plainly: "for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials" (1 Peter 1:6). But he says those trials show the proven character of their faith, which is "more precious than gold" (1 Peter 1:7). I spent years in the back of a drawer, so I'll tell you, the dark season is not the end of the story.

Then Peter points to the prophets who searched carefully, and to the angels who "long to look into these things" (1 Peter 1:10-12). If all that attention is on this salvation, then your faith in a Jesus you haven't seen is no small thing, friend. You love Him and believe in Him, and Peter says you're receiving "the salvation of your souls" (1 Peter 1:8-9). So keep your ovens warm and your eyes up, because the hope you have is alive.
